title: Image slider
description:
Write the function `imageSlider(images)` in plain TypeScript, without a framework. It adds an image slider to the page: one image at a time from a list, and two buttons, **Previous** and **Next**, for moving through the list. ### Rules & clarifications - The function receives `images`, a list of image URLs (`string[]`) with at least one element, and adds the slider to the `` of the page. - There is a single `` element. At the start, its `src` is the first URL in `images`. - Under the image there are two buttons with the texts `Previous` and `Next`, in this order. - When the **Next** button is clicked, the `src` of the image changes to the next URL in the list. When the **Previous** button is clicked, it changes to the previous URL. - The **Previous** button is disabled while the first image is shown. The **Next** button is disabled while the last image is shown. - The tests check the behaviour, not the styling: no CSS is needed. - The rendered HTML has this structure: ```html
``` ### Examples For a list `images` with 3 URLs: - At the start, the first image is shown, **Previous** is disabled and **Next** is enabled. - Click **Next** twice → the third image is shown and **Next** is disabled. - Then click **Previous** once → the second image is shown and both buttons are enabled.
